L’histoire inspire, si on en croit la po: History inspires, if poet Excel’N’cia, pen name of Nancia Marthe, is to be believed
La poète Excel’N’cia, nom de plume de Na: Poet Excel’N’cia, pen name of Nancia Marthe. Photo: Ridolphe Aristil
L’histoire inspire, si on en croit la po: History inspires, if poet Excel’N’cia, pen name of Nancia Marthe, is to be believed. Last summer, our team filmed her in Montréal-Nord as she recited Chers descendants, a text of her own. “The goal of my poetry is to learn about our history myself, to be able to make it accessible, to open the door to a conversation so that we can learn more,” says the performer. Her piece, composed a year earlier, grew out of feelings that came to a head after the death of George Floyd and other fatal incidents of police violence against Black people, in a year that reignited tensions.
« À l’époque, j’avais beaucoup d’émotion: “At the time, I had a lot of negative emotions, sadness, frustration about the injustice that still exists, despite years of struggle,” the poet tells us. Today, she wants to express more optimism by talking about history.
« J’ai utilisé cette pièce à la fois pou: “I used this piece both to promote our history and to try to bring a positive touch, a note of hope,” says the young woman. In doing so, she addresses her descendants while also evoking her ancestors.
« J’imagine qu’avant tout, ce qu’on fait: “I guess, above all, what we do, through community involvement, is that we're able to change things ourselves. It's like I needed to convince myself of that so that things would improve, while convincing my audience too,” she confides. Nancia talks about history, but also about identity.
« En cherchant à me définir, à savoir qu: “In trying to define myself, to figure out who I am, I tried to understand what the history of Black people in Canada was, where they came from, whether there was slavery here. I wanted to know the journey of Black Canadians,” she adds, referring to a historical perspective that was left out of her history books at school. For the poet, it's not enough to look back; we have to take action.
« Je crois que, maintenant, il est impor: “I believe that now, it's important to come out of lockdown little by little, to start acting again. We can't just sit there, take part in online debates, write on virtual walls,” says the poet, who invites everyone to get involved. “Because the difference [is made] through actions, discussions, by reaching out to others. By staying isolated, with physical distancing, we cultivate fear, fear of the other. I think we have to push back against that. I encourage you to do so.”
